notes.title: An Interview with the Creator of While Waiting
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/234eaf5ab7c58551b564bcc0c45c12a9b9007dc8.png[/img]

While Waiting is, in fact, a long dream. 

In it, Adam experiences his entire life and what the future has in store for him. When players restart the game, everything resets and begins anew. So no matter what Adam does, he always reaches the same ending. This shows the theme of our game, which is like determinism. So like everything is determined.
The reason the setting is Times Square, NY is because, as most people know, the main “New Year's Eve celebration” in the US and is one of the most iconic celebrations in the world. In the game, we have several New Year levels. It is more like the ending of the chapter, where players can see Adam grow up later. This is why the first level, the New Year level, is in Times Square. So that's why.


We hope players will learn to accept and embrace their life and discard the attachment. The game includes so many stickers, but aside from the “doing nothing” sticker, none of them actually affect the game's progress in any way. Some stickers are designed to be very, very difficult, and in most levels, it's impossible to collect them in one run. That's because we intentionally make it difficult and want the players to learn how to give up.


Here's a short story: 
So when I was young, I loved playing games, especially JRPGs. But as I get older, I was trying to complete every side quest. I know what the structures of these games are, and I tried to get all the achievements, but I never had the same feeling when I was playing JRPGs as a child. It became more like a complete to-do list. An attachment. This kind of attachment made it hard for me to truly enjoy the game.


The intention behind making this game was to help players learn to let go, to experience a game with just their pure heart, feel free, and not care too much about the ending. Just enjoy the game itself. Yes, it's a very simple thing and pretty hard to do, but that is how we designed the game and hope players can take away from While Waiting.


We hope you continue to find the game inspirational and find joy in life while being patient 🙂

Sincerely,

[b]- The While Waiting Team[/b]

notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We're excited to share some awesome improvements coming with our upcoming v1.0.2 update! Here's what you can look forward to:

[h2]New Features[/h2]

[h3]Patience Meter:[/h3] Many levels now include a new patience meter that depletes when you use a fidget toy. Once it’s empty, you'll have the option to skip the current level—giving you more control over your play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/61ce0ea627c60d8c3bff6442a9d8380e5dfb13f5.png[/img]

[h2]General Fixes and Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] You can now pause the game or even restart a level when the notebook isn't available, ensuring you never miss a beat.
[*] Control improvements have been made—you can now use the enter and arrow keys to play.
[*] We've fixed some pesky UI issues so that level items stay behind important interface elements.
[/list]
[h2]Specific level bugs have been fixed[/h2]
[list]
[*] Level 54, "Wait for her to arrive": The player character’s odd walking behavior at the end of the level has been corrected.
[*] Level 93, "Wait for your turn to play mahjong": The disappearing initial tile in mahjong has been resolved.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/5ddeda3d2558a812caf240157e29480183fc5cc8.png[/img]
Looking ahead, our next update will address some interaction feel issues, including adding mouse control for several levels.
We hope these changes make your gameplay smoother and more enjoyable. As always, thank you for your continued support and feedback. Stay tuned for more updates and happy gaming!

If you're still unsure, don’t just take our word for it—let’s take a look at what reviewers have been saying!

"It’s rare for a game to capture the small, seemingly insignificant moments of life and turn them into a core gameplay loop. Yet, While Waiting does just that—and does it well."

notes.title: While Waiting - First Update Patch Notes!
notes.content:
Hello, dear players!

Thank you for playing While Waiting! We've been closely monitoring your feedback and working hard to bring improvements, bug fixes, and  updates. Here’s what’s new in our first post-launch update:

[h2]General Fixes & Improvements[/h2]
Fixed an issue where the game screen would display incorrectly if your system resolution was smaller than the resolution set by the game.
Added mouse scroll support for the level selection panel.
After finishing the True Ending, the "Start" button on the title screen will now appear as "Start?" You can retrieve your notebook by clicking it.

[h2]Level-Specific Fixes & Adjustments[/h2]
Level 003 - Wait for the toaster: Fixed a bug where thrown cereals landed in the wrong position.
Level 014 - Wait for the award to be announced: Fixed a bug where the player character could clip out of the area.
Level 025 - Wait for the shooting star: The "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star" sticker can now be unlocked with the correct sequence of tapping, rather than drawing a correct sequence of lines.
Level 029 - Wait for the admission email: Fixed a bug where email items sometimes overlapped.
Level 035 - Wait for your turn to buy lunch: The "My Burgeria" sticker now unlocks after making one burger instead of five.
Level 043 - Wait to forget her: Reduced the time length and made stickers easier to obtain.
Level 054 - Wait for her to arrive: Fixed various bugs related to the popcorn machine.
Level 067 - Wait for the vicar to finish the talk: The "I read carefully" sticker is now easier to unlock, with additional hints.
Level 095 - Wait for your daughter to visit you: Increased hand movement speed; fixed a bug where hands in different split screens moved simultaneously; reduced overall level duration.
Level 098 - Wait to finish the IV drip: Reduced overall level duration.

[h2]For Content Creators: [/h2]
The music in While Waiting consists of open-source, public domain classical pieces. We've done our best to avoid tracks that could trigger copyright claims, but since classical compositions can sound very similar, some may still get muted when posting videos on YouTube or Twitch. To prevent this, we recommend streaming with the background music turned off.

Thank you for your continued support and feedback! We hope these changes improve your While Waiting experience. Let us know if you encounter any other issues or have suggestions — we're always listening!

Happy waiting!

notes.title: Doing nothing
notes.content:
Hey everyone. Happy new year! 👋
It’s time for another behind the scene at the development of While Waiting. Today, we’re diving into one of the most exciting aspects of game creation: gameplay design! 

[h2]The Concept: Doing nothing 🌱[/h2]
When we first started working on While Waiting, our goal was to create a game that felt both introspective and engaging. The idea was to capture moments of life — those times when you’re just waiting for something to happen, but you still find ways to make the time meaningful. It’s about finding something to do to kill time, like noticing the world around you, helping someone in need, or simply listening to the sounds of the environment. But why are we doing that?

[h2]Meet our protagonist[/h2]
Adam is an ordinary human being, waiting for over 100 situations throughout his life. 
As a child, Adam always fools around but also has a lot of imagination.
As a young man, Adam will experience student life, first loves, and his first parties with his roommate Johnny.
Studies are over, and Adam enters the workforce. Strange things begin to happen—could it be due to fatigue or the passage of time?
It will be up to the players to discover what happens next to Adam as he ages and moves through different stages of life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/4b951852eed18829f9bb235430b1eadccff291ff.png[/img]

[h2]A puzzle-game but not only.[/h2]
The core gameplay of While Waiting revolves around exploration and puzzle-solving. 

Each scene/situation is detailed as in real life and encourages players to take their time to explore the environment. Of course, they can wait and do nothing, but for those who want to keep busy, several challenges await them. A notebook indicates what they can do in each scene in order to collect stickers and make the time pass faster. 

[h2]The Adventure of Life[/h2]
Behind the comedic appearance, players experience a real adventure.
Immerse yourself in a unique blend of comedic reactions and a thought-provoking narrative that delves deep into the profound aspects of life.

How do you react to doing nothing? Is doing nothing a waste of time, or a good opportunity to take care of your mental health, to refocus on what matters to you? As children, we are often impatient, but as we grow up, how does our perception of time change?

[h2]Replayability.[/h2]
While Waiting offers great replayability because it is impossible to collect all the stickers at once.
Puzzles are challenging but never frustrating, ensuring a smooth flow of gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/5969181dda297ad4a4847e9794fdd76675f8f2b1.jpg[/img]

[h2]Emotional Storytelling[/h2]
While Waiting also has emotional storytelling. The narrative tackles themes of friendship, love, family, loneliness, loss and self-discovery will resonate with players.

The game invites laughter, joy, and introspection!
Thank you again for supporting us and don’t forget : until next time, happy gaming!

notes.title: The Inspirations Behind While Waiting and Its Evolving Art Style
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We hope you're all doing great! It's been a while since we talked, and today we’re taking a break from development to share something a little different. While Waiting has unique art style and we would like to show you how it’s evolved over time. So, let’s dive into a bit of a behind-the-scenes look at how While Waiting came to life and where we drew our inspiration from.

[b]The Origins[/b]
At the very first, we were trying to figure out a bold, recognizable, yet funny art direction. The flat color was our first approach. But later on we thought it would be too similar to Moncage (our first game)? We wished to try something different. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/09cd24ff3502d8a2530cc6fddb23a777544651ab.png[/img]

We had a Picasso phase and then an illustration one. Le style commençait à s'affiner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/fb5502217ee99d451cf32327519d733b69f749c7.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/cd742beb986f648f8a9c4c2f571c3b26ae19bd78.png[/img]

[b]The Evolution: Finding Our Unique Style[/b]
In the beginning, we experimented a lot — our art board was filled with different concepts. But as development continued, we found ourselves drawn to a more comic line art style. 
We also wanted to create a sense of timelessness — something that looks modern but feels like it could be from any era. To achieve this, we focused on the pastel color palette. Our backgrounds are deliberately simple, allowing characters and gameplay elements to take center stage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/c79f00c7efd46b5492577b08ec9a95f2deb40ce8.png[/img]

That's how we ended up with this clean, playful, yet unique art direction!

Stay tuned for more updates, and don’t forget to share your let’s play and screenshot of the demo with us using #WhileWaiting and https://x.com/PlayOptillusion on social media. We love seeing your posts!

Thank You, from the Bottom of Our Hearts <3 

Until next time, happy gaming,
The While Waiting Team

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44166345/2142746124b444e0ccbe605e1cd592ba43a772a8.png[/img]

[h2]Transition Levels[/h2]

The game explores the passage of time and life through Adam’s journey, reflected not only in the scenarios he finds himself in but also in subtle details, like the growth of a plant. This plant grows slowly over time as you progress through the game, symbolizing life’s progression and the inevitable passage of time—mirroring Adam’s own story. notes.title: While Waiting challenges you to make your own fidgety fun as you puzzle through life's little pauses
notes.content:
What do you reach for when you're waiting in line at the supermarket, or waiting in a shop doorway for the rain to stop, or even while you're waiting for a game to finish downloading? I don't mean to assume, but let's face it, it's probably your phone, where some idle doomscrolling likely awaits you, or some other, time-wasting distraction that will help fill the dead air between one task and the next. Well, While Waiting is a game that delves into precisely this fundamental human question: what is the best thing to do while waiting for something else to happen? It's from the makers of the very good puzzle game Moncage, and its newly released Steam demo is a pure, fidgety brilliance.

Read more
